_note: Spreading by Word of Mouth: bare previs of the stoa and festival ground (set 'stoa', colonnade at explorer (266, 8)) and the libraries (set 'libraries'). No cast: the image pass adds the people; each note is the picture's brief.

cover.note: The stoa's colonnade at mid-morning with the festival ground before it: pairs of scholars in plain wool chitons stand talking in the colonnade, one holding out a scrap of papyrus to another, and on the ground pairs of copyists sit facing each other across the long tables with scrolls between them.

scene.prompt: Photorealistic photograph from a height, Hellenistic Greece, 3rd century BC. Keep [image 1]'s camera, framing and layout exactly, but none of its surfaces survive: every faceted green shape becomes real olive, pine or cypress foliage, every flat pale surface real weathered limestone or lime plaster, the flat blue a real sea. Clear bright Aegean sun. The buildings in [image 1] are finished models: keep every modelled part of the stoa (its plain drum columns, frieze, tiled lean-to roof, back wall and bench) and every stone table and bench on the levelled ground before it exactly where it is, give each its real material, add no architecture. Mid-morning. Pairs of scholars in plain wool chitons like [image 2]'s man stand talking in the colonnade, one holding out a small scrap of papyrus to another; at the long tables pairs of copyists sit facing each other with scrolls unrolled between them. Nobody stands apart or presides. Beaten earth ground, olive trees and cypresses behind. No writing, no signs.

p01-library.note: One of the coast's libraries seen from its porch road: a small plastered building with a gabled tile roof and a columned porch, olive trees round it. A reader stands at the door with a scroll under his arm.

scene.prompt: Photorealistic architectural photograph, Hellenistic Greece, 3rd century BC, from the path before a small library. Keep [image 1]'s camera, framing and layout exactly, but none of its surfaces survive: every faceted green shape becomes real olive, pine or cypress foliage, every flat pale surface real weathered limestone or lime plaster, the flat blue a real sea. Clear bright Aegean sun. The buildings in [image 1] are finished models: keep every modelled part of the library: its dressed stone base, plastered walls, porch of two plain unfluted columns, pediment, steps, open door and every roof tile exactly where it is, give each its real material, add no architecture. Weathered lime plaster, terracotta tiles, a worn dirt path to the steps. Through the open door a dim room with wooden racks of papyrus scrolls. A reader in a grey chiton like [image 2]'s man stands at the door with a scroll under his arm. Olive trees and pines round the clearing. No writing, no statues.

p02-festival.note: The festival ground below the stoa on the day of the festival: rows of long stone tables, at each a pair of copyists facing each other, a scroll unrolled between them, each running a finger down a column while the other follows on his own copy.

p03-stoa.note: Scholars in the stoa's colonnade: travellers in dusty cloaks have just arrived and are telling those they meet, in ones and twos, what they carry on a scrap of papyrus. Nobody stands in the middle; nobody is in charge.

p04-coast.note: The coast from the air: libraries scattered among olive groves and joined by footpaths, the stoa and its festival ground at the water's edge. A courier is on one path.
